message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine crimes based on facts. The defendant stole many motorcycles, other items, including military ammunition, firearms? Actually bullets, rifle ammo, etc. Also stole cash, jewelry, etc. So crimes: theft (盗窃). Also illegal possession of firearms/ammunition? He stole military bullets, but does that constitute illegal possession of firearms? He stole bullets, but not necessarily possession of firearms. Could be illegal possession of ammunition (非法持有枪支、弹药) but he didn't have gun, only bullets. Might be illegal possession of ammunition (非法持有弹药). However typical Chinese criminal law: illegal possession of firearms, ammunition, explosives is a crime. So could be "非法持有、私藏枪支、弹药" but he didn't have gun, only bullets and a rifle? He had a rifle? No, only bullets, a rifle? He stole a rifle? Not mentioned. So maybe "非法持有弹药" but classification may be "非法持有、私藏枪支、弹药" as a combined offense. Also "抢夺"? No, he stole items, not using force. So theft.

Also "诈骗"? No.

Also "非法占有" is part of theft.

Also "盗窃数额巨大" qualifies as theft.

Also "非法持有弹药" qualifies as illegal possession of ammunition.

Thus answer: 盗窃;非法持有弹药 (or illegal possession of firearms and ammunition). In examples they used "非法持有、私藏枪支、弹药". So we can list both.

Thus final answer: [罪名]盗窃;非法持有、私藏枪支、弹药<eoa>
